Password cracking algorithms are designed to test all possible combinations of characters—common methods include brute force, dictionary attacks, and timing analysis.

**Brute force:** Start with common passwords and iterate through character combinations until a match is found. An algorithm can test billions of possibilities in seconds.

**Dictionary attacks:** Instead of brute force, use a pre-computed list of word lists and try every word within those lists. This is a practical first step for many password-cracking tools.

**Timing analysis:** Attackers measure how long it takes to find a match (execution time, memory access, CPU cycles). Longer-lived passwords (password-cracking-related systems) suffer from this timing side-channel.
